subject: Redwood OpenAI-compat & hyperscaler comparison - next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Smith <daniel.smith@acme.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood OpenAI-compat & hyperscaler comparison - next tests

Thanks again for the call this morning 	6 great to meet the Acme team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate migration/compatibility and the performance picture relative to the hyperscalers.

Recap (from our discovery)
- Current plan: prototype migration of your ticket summarization and search assistant to a self-hosted/managed inference stack.
- Primary goals: API parity with minimal code changes, predictable latency at peak, and unit-cost that meets your SRE budget.
- Constraints: PCI-scope data on certain routes (we discussed VPC/Private deployment later).

What we propose next (30–60 day test plan)
1) SDK swap smoke test (goal: minimal code change)
   - Objective: Replace OpenAI SDK calls with Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoint; confirm identical outputs on representative prompt set (prompt set attached).
   - Deliverable: Pull request + runnable example in Node and Python (we'll provide).

2) Functional parity checks
   - Same prompt, model params (temp/stop tokens/top_p), same system prompt handling.
   - Record diffs: token accounting, stop behavior, sampling variance across N=20 runs.

3) Latency and cost baseline vs hyperscaler
   - Controlled runs against your sample workload (we'll provide synthetic traffic scripts).
   - Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, cost per 1K tokens, error rates.

4) Streaming and error-handling tests
   - Confirm SSE/WebSocket streaming parity and reconnect semantics.

5) Security/compliance checklist
   - Evidence for audit: network topology, KMS integration, logs retention (we'll supply checklist).

Attachments: redwood-openai-compat-test-plan.pdf, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-comp.xlsx

Proposed immediate next steps
- We'll stand up a short-lived test org and issue a temporary API key for you to try the SDK swap (ETA: same day).
- If you're comfortable, schedule a 30-min workshop where we run the smoke test together and iterate on any prompt differences.

Availability: I'm free tomorrow 9–11am PT or Friday 1–4pm PT.

If there's anyone else on your side who should be looped in for procurement/proc/infra, please let me know.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Great questions — answers below and I've provisioned a test org for you.

Short answers:
- Test org: acme-test-20261016 (temporary), Test API key: rwi_test_abc123 (expires 7 days) — do not use for production.
- Streaming: Yes — we support both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming. Example snippets attached in compat-code-snippets.zip.
- Target models: start with our openai-compatible names mapping to the approx. capabilities you mentioned: gpt-4o -> rwi-g4o-compat, gpt-4o-mini -> rwi-g4o-mini-compat. We'll provide exact model mapping and known differences in the test-plan PDF.

What I've attached/linked:
- compat-code-snippets.zip (Node/Python examples for SDK swap)
- redwood-openai-compat-test-plan.pdf (detailed test plan)
- redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-comp.xlsx (baseline checklist + sample metrics)
- HubSpot test record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/987654321

Next operational steps:
1) Run the SDK swap smoke test using the provided key and the attached Node example (should be ~5 lines changed).
2) Run the 20-run sampling check from the test-plan against rwi-g4o-compat and gpt-4o to compare sampling variance.
3) Share any prompt diffs you see — we'll log them and iterate (typical fixes are tokenization differences or stop-sequence behavior).

Would you prefer the 30-min workshop tomorrow at 10am PT? If yes we'll send a calendar invite and have Rishi join to run the latency/cost baseline scripts with you.

Thanks — looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
